summary.headline: Patanjali Foods Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR11,323 crores, but operating EBITDA margin fell to 3.76% on edible oil pressure.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations reached a record INR11,323 crores in Q2 FY27, up 16% YoY, with operating EBITDA of INR426 crores (3.76%) and PBT of INR409 crores (3.59%). H1 revenue was INR22,660 crores (up 22%), with EBITDA of INR969 crores (4.28%). Edible oil drove growth, with revenue up 22% to a record INR8,532 crores but margin at 3%, while the food staples and ethnic foods businesses were weak and management chose to de-grow staples. Management flagged softer rural demand, rising inflation (CPI 6.09% in October) and a later festive calendar, and said the festive season has since gained momentum.

segments.name: Edible oil
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR8,532 crores (record, up 22% YoY) at 3% EBITDA margin; H1 revenue INR17,037 crores (up 25%) at 4.11% margin. Volume growth about 3.9% in Q2 per management correction; H1 volume 11.07 lakh tons (corrected), up about 10.5%.

segments.name: Oil palm plantation
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR742 crores. Cultivated area 1,27,265 ha out of 6.63 lakh ha allocated; about 34% of area in prime yielding phase, about 8% young, about 57% immature.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR638 crores (up 28% YoY), EBITDA margin 11.91%; H1 revenue INR1,198 crores (up 28%), margin 13.52%. Volume about 56,122 tons vs 49,874 tons in Q1 (up 12.53% per correction); growth mainly volume-led, Doodh biscuits about 85% of portfolio.

segments.name: Staples (food)
segments.commentary: Revenue cut to INR838 crores from INR1,110 crores in Q1 as a deliberate de-growth; EBITDA INR15.61 crores (1.86%) vs negative INR59 crores in Q1.

segments.name: Ethnic foods (Nutrela)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR525 crores (up about 14% QoQ from INR460 crores); EBITDA INR16.78 crores (3.19%) vs 1.89% in Q1, still below management's 8-10% food margin target.

segments.name: Skincare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR187 crores in Q2 (corrected from INR188 crores), up about 25.6% YoY and 13.8% QoQ, almost entirely volume-led.

segments.name: Dental care (Dant Kanti)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR378 crores, up about 16% QoQ from INR325 crores in Q1 and about 4.5% YoY (corrected); H1 dental INR704 crores, up 9%.

segments.name: Textured soya
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR186 crores, volume growth 16% YoY; H1 INR345 crores (up 15%).

segments.name: Ghee
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR306 crores; H1 INR525 crores. Management expects demand to strengthen through winter and wedding season.

guidance_outlook: Management expects HPC to close FY27 with about 15% growth and H2 to be better than H1.
Expects commodity inflation (wheat, sugar, milk, soybean, crude-linked inputs, freight) to continue in the near term.
Targets food margins of 8-10% over time; sees staples and ethnic foods margin improving from Q3 as price increases and volume pickup take hold.
Festive season momentum in October and November is seen as a positive lead into the wedding season; winter expected to support demand.
Oil palm maturing plantations expected to add a growing earnings stream over a few years.
Inorganic opportunities are being evaluated selectively; nothing currently in pipeline for near-term investment.
capex_capacity: Oil palm: 1,27,265 ha cultivated as of 30 Sep 2026 against 6.63 lakh ha allocated; 223 FFB collection and farmer centres, 49 nurseries, MoUs with 12 state governments.
Submitted expression of interest for oil palm development in Bihar under the National Mission on Edible Oils.

Indore (Mangliya) integrated plant to be relocated because land is now in a residential area; the company took a lease on 42.5 acres from parent Patanjali Ayurved, which paid MPSIDC earlier. Lease premium paid is INR185 crores.
Biscuit distribution: about 3 lakh direct outlets, with indirect reach estimated at about 1.5 times that.
demand_pricing: Edible oil: H1 volume growth about 10.5% (11.07 lakh tons vs 9.99 lakh tons); Q2 volume 5.0 lakh tons vs 5.22 lakh tons in Q2 FY26 (corrected). Most revenue growth came from unit price increases.
Govt cut effective import duty on crude palm and soybean oil from 16.5% to 11% and on crude sunflower oil to 5.5% on 24 Sep 2026; the company says it is passing the benefit to consumers.
Competition in dental care intensified (new launches, pricing, variants); Dant Kanti extended into toothbrushes and variants.
Herbal toothpaste market about one-third of total toothpaste; management says it is consolidating among two or three players and growing about 10-12%.
Urban demand resilient, rural muted amid CPI rising from 4.45% (July) to 6.09% (October); food inflation 8.94%. Monsoon rainfall deficit 13%.
Skincare and biscuits price increases limited; growth driven by distribution expansion into unmet markets.

qa_highlights.question: Has competitive intensity in toothpaste and biscuits changed over the last few quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Dental competition has intensified on launches, pricing and variants. Dant Kanti grew to INR378 crores in Q2 from INR325 crores in Q1 (about 16%), and management said the brand is competitive due to new toothbrush and variant extensions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering inorganic acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating selectively for distribution or portfolio gaps, but seller price expectations have been too high; nothing is on the cards for near-term investment.

qa_highlights.question: Volume versus price split for biscuits, skincare and edible oil?
qa_highlights.answer: Biscuits are largely volume-led with no price increase, about 80-85% Doodh biscuits. Edible oil volume grew about 3.9% with the rest from price; skincare is mostly volume-led, up 25.6% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why are staples and ethnic foods declining?
qa_highlights.answer: Management chose to de-grow staples to protect margin (revenue INR838 crores, EBITDA 1.86%). Ethnic foods grew to INR525 crores with margin 3.19%, and management expects margins to improve from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Any inventory loss from the edible oil duty cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact was marginal and fully booked in the quarter, as material was in bonded warehouses or afloat; the EBITDA drop from 5.22% to 3% reflected the duty change.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the lease transfer from Patanjali Ayurved for the Indore land at INR185 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: The Indore plant is being relocated because the land is now residential. The lease premium is paid to the parent, which paid MPSIDC earlier, and rental is minimal; treasury income impact is expected to be small.

risks_watch: Edible oil margin of 3% and post-duty-cut pass-through; watch whether the lower duty supports affordability and volume.
Commodity inflation in staples, ethnic foods and Nutrela; the target 8-10% food margin is far away.
Rural demand softness, CPI at 6.09% (October), and a 13% monsoon deficit affecting Kharif and Rabi.
Intensifying dental competition, with the leader and others raising launches and pricing.
Edible oil pack-size standardisation (three-month transition) could affect demand; management says no financial impact.
Corrections to several figures in the call (Q2 edible oil volume, Q1 volume, biscuit growth) suggest disclosure accuracy to verify against the filed data.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and HPC targets, but cautious on food margins and rural demand. Management was candid about commodity pressure and the staples de-growth. Several numbers were corrected during Q&A, and some answers were deferred to follow-up.
key_quotes: We expect to close the year at what has been a broad basis, 15% growth in the HPC.

So staples, for example, we took a conscious decision to de-grow, because it was just not making sense, because the ability to pass on a lot of staples, food pricing onto the consumers was very challenging.
Oil palm is a long-term annuity-style business with high margin returns that strengthens our backward integration.
but yes, as you can see that our EBITDA from 5.22% dropped to 3%

adds.what: Indore (Mangliya) integrated plant relocation; leased 42.5 acres from parent Patanjali Ayurved, lease premium INR185 crores
Oil palm plantation: 1,27,265 ha cultivated of 6.63 lakh ha allocated; ~57% immature, ~34% prime yielding
Oil palm expression of interest in Bihar under National Mission on Edible Oils

growth.why: Management guides HPC to about 15% growth for FY27 with H2 better than H1, and sees staples and ethnic foods margins improving from Q3 via price increases and volume pickup; backing is partial (HPC distribution, pricing, volume pickup) with no specific new capacity or order numbers, while the plantation and Indore relocation are long-dated and not growth drivers this year.

oneOffs.what: Edible oil duty cut on 24 Sep 2026 passed to consumers; management said inventory impact was marginal and fully booked in Q2, so it is a one-off in the margin compression rather than a growth gain

quality.why: Q2 revenue grew 16% YoY, with edible oil (INR8,532 crores, up 22%) the main contributor, but Q2 edible oil volume was only about 3.9% (5.0 lakh tons vs 5.22 lakh tons in Q2 FY26 per the correction), so most of that growth came from price; biscuits (+28%) and skincare (+25.6%) were volume-led, while staples were cut to INR838 crores from INR1,110 crores in Q1 as a deliberate de-growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 3.76% (Q1 5.22%) on edible oil at 3% margin after the duty cut, but management expects staples and ethnic foods margins to improve from Q3 via price increases, and targets 8-10% food margins over time; Nutrela is at 3.19% and staples at 1.86%, so the path is long.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant is commissioned in the window: the Indore plant is being relocated (lease premium INR185 crores) and oil palm is 57% immature, so the plantation adds earnings only over a few years, with no near-term capacity coming live.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 edible oil volume is up about 10.5% to 11.07 lakh tons and biscuit volume rose 12.5% QoQ to 56,122 tons, with HPC guided to about 15% growth in FY27 and H2 better than H1; rural demand is muted (CPI 6.09%, monsoon deficit 13%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Oil palm expansion continues (1,27,265 ha cultivated of 6.63 lakh ha allocated; Bihar expression of interest submitted), but management says inorganic deals are not in the pipeline and the call gives no utilisation figure to drive a new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is holding guidance (HPC 15%, food margin 8-10% construct) amid 3% edible oil margin, commodity inflation expected to continue, and a rural slowdown, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Commodity inflation (wheat, sugar, milk, soybean, crude-linked inputs, freight) is expected to persist, staples and Nutrela margins are still far below the 8-10% target, and dental competition is intensifying (Dant Kanti up only 4.5% YoY).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Dant Kanti has extended into toothbrushes and variants and skincare is growing 25.6% YoY, but the call names no specific dated launch.

rows.label: Edible oil duty-cut pass-through
rows.why: Import duty on crude palm and soybean oil was cut from 16.5% to 11% on 24 Sep 2026 and the company says it is passing the benefit to consumers, after edible oil margin fell from 5.22% to 3%; whether this restores margin or supports volume is unproven.

rows.label: Festive and wedding-season demand
rows.why: Management says festive momentum in October and November is positive, with winter and the wedding season expected to lift ghee and HPC demand; ghee H1 revenue is INR525 crores.

rows.label: Indore land lease premium
rows.why: A INR185 crore lease premium was paid to parent Patanjali Ayurved for the relocated Indore plant, which is a cash outflow, though management says treasury impact is expected to be small.

tone.note: Management was confident on HPC (about 15% growth for FY27) and on festive momentum, but cautious on food margins, commodity inflation and rural demand, and it was candid about the staples de-growth.
